synthesis:
scout:record-check-ins exhausted production host memory (~29 GB marginal, 17 concurrent processes, ~30 GB headroom) and forced a host reboot on 2026-08-12. The command's own architecture is the amplifier: per org it pulls the ENTIRE open-order address list (hundreds of thousands of rows for the largest orgs/hotlists) out of ClickHouse into a PHP array, holds it live across a 43-kit loop, array_chunk()-copies the whole array once per kit, re-serializes each chunk as a ClickHouse values() literal, and accumulates every match in an unbounded $matches[] — so per-process memory is O(addresses_per_org), not O(matches). A second defect (withoutOverlapping(10) is a lock EXPIRY, not a duration cap) lets concurrency grow unboundedly whenever a cycle outlives 10 minutes, which it always does (36-148 min observed) — turning a bounded-but-large per-process footprint into O(addresses x concurrency), which is what actually took the host down. A third, independent defect (lower(kit_mapping) defeats the sc_positions primary key) inflates cycle duration and is what feeds the concurrency growth. The schedule is currently commented out in production and stays that way until the fix lands. 

The intended outcome (this repo's share of the fix, W2+W3): rewrite the matcher so the match is computed entirely server-side in ClickHouse by lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's already-correct CTE architecture (bbox-prefiltered geoDistance join, open-hotlist + address-link resolution, EWKT parsing) adapted from clarity.scans_{hot,cold} to clarity.sc_positions, so only the ~40 match rows per cycle ever cross into PHP — eliminating both the round-trip amplifier and the unbounded accumulator. Pair that with a hard concurrency ceiling that holds independent of runtime (W3), a production-cardinality memory regression test (AC6), a fix for the fact that ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows every failure to [] making a dead ClickHouse indistinguishable from a quiet cycle (AC7), and a parity test proving the rewritten matcher agrees with ScoutCheckInRollupQuery on identical inputs (AC9). The sc_positions primary-key fix (W1) is chlocal-owned and does not ship here; re-enabling the schedule (W4) is an operational, prod-only step gated on host memory verification after W1-W3 land.

scope.summary: Rewrite the two-query recorder path (ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery + ScoutCheckInMatchQuery, orchestrated by ScoutRecordCheckIns) into a single server-side-computed match per org/kit, by lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's CTE (its docblock names this exact extension point as DEV-1758's intended lift). Add a concurrency ceiling in the command (W3), a peak-memory regression test at prod-representative address cardinality (AC6), an explicit failed-vs-empty signal around the ClickhouseQuery swallow-to-[] behavior (AC7), and a parity test against ScoutCheckInRollupQuery (AC9). The schedule stays commented out; W1 (chlocal projection) is not touched.

proposed_changes.change: Replace the values()-injection + array_chunk architecture with a single CTE per call (org or kit — design risk 1, unresolved) that lifts ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's shape: position_window (clarity.sc_positions, lower(kit_mapping), bbox) INNER JOIN addresses (open_hotlists -> zod.public_hotlist_address -> zod.public_address, id-IN-pruned + EWKT-parsed) ON geoDistance(...) <= 160.934, GROUP BY (address_id, hour_bucket) with the same argMin/argMin-tuple dedup. No PHP address array, no addressValues() literal builder, no ADDRESS_CHUNK.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1 — eliminate the PHP<->CH round-trip amplifier that is the primary duration and memory driver.

proposed_changes.change: Decision point, not a guaranteed change: once matches are computed server-side, the recorder no longer needs the org's full address list in PHP, so this class may become unused by ScoutRecordCheckIns (confirmed via grep: its only callers today are the command and its own test). Either delete it or repurpose it (e.g. only for a diagnostics/backfill path) — do not leave a dead, uncalled class silently.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1 — its entire purpose (materializing an address list for PHP-side re-injection) goes away under the server-side rewrite.

proposed_changes.change: Drop the openOrderAddressesForOrg() call and the $addresses parameter threading through recordCheckInsForKit(); call the rewritten matcher directly per kit (or per org, per design risk 1) and bulk-write results via ScoutCheckIn::query()->insertOrIgnore($rows) against the existing unique(kit_id, address_id, hour_bucket) instead of a per-match firstOrCreate() loop. Add a hard concurrency ceiling at command start (W3) — an N-slot semaphore that exits early with no slot, or per-org queued dispatch with an explicitly-set HORIZON_SUPERVISOR_*_PROCESSES (config/horizon.php currently defaults maxProcesses to 1 on the {low}-queue supervisor, which would silently serialize a naive job fan-out — exactly what sank the prior DEV-2347 attempt). Add an explicit failed-vs-empty signal per org/kit for AC7 rather than relying on an empty return array.
proposed_changes.reason: AC1, AC3, AC4, AC7 — the command is where the accumulator lived and where concurrency must now be bounded.

proposed_changes.change: Distinguish 'ran, empty' from 'failed' for AC7. ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows every \Throwable to [] in production|testing (ClickhouseQuery.php:29-37), so a dead ClickHouse and a legitimately-empty match set are byte-for-byte identical to the caller today — measured in production as 94 CH-159 errors against 0 'enumeration failed' warnings in a 4h window. Needs a signal that does not depend on catching an exception the base class already ate (e.g. a sentinel/exception variant surfaced through a new query method, or a metric emitted from inside handle() before the base class's catch).

questions.q: Per-org batch (lower(kit_mapping) IN (...)) vs per-kit equality (lower(kit_mapping) = ?) for the rewritten matcher — the IN form risks the optimizer ignoring the prefix-prune (~12 vs ~43 queries/cycle), and the evidence file says explicitly this must be 'settled with EXPLAIN', preferring more queries over losing the prune.

Will ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's CTE shape (tuned for scans arriving on plate-read cadence) perform acceptably against sc_positions, whose GPS fixes arrive roughly every 3 seconds — a much larger position_window and a less selective bbox? The brief flags this as unmeasured, not assumed-safe.

W3 concurrency-ceiling mechanism: an N-slot semaphore acquired at command start, or per-org queued jobs (Horizon)? Queued jobs default maxProcesses=1 on the {low} supervisor (config/horizon.php:198-208), which is exactly what made the prior DEV-2347 job-dispatch attempt cut throughput ~7x and get reverted (commit 102a3430) — any queued-job design must set HORIZON_SUPERVISOR_2_PROCESSES deliberately, but the ticket leaves the choice open.

Should ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery be deleted once the recorder no longer calls it, or kept for a future non-recorder caller? No other caller exists today (confirmed via grep: only ScoutRecordCheckIns and its own test reference it), and DEV-2339's precedent note anticipates but does not resolve this.

How do AC2 (duration measured) and AC8 (host pct_usable verified) get satisfied given this pipeline has no production or ClickHouse Cloud access? The evidence file's own rollout plan (Canary EXPLAIN, query_log comparison, post-re-enable host watch) is entirely a human/ops-and-prod-access activity.
Should the app.experimental.clarity_scout flag / schedule stay disabled after W2+W3+the ACs implementable here land, until W1 (chlocal projection) also ships?

notes: Binding hazards to preserve when lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's CTE (all called out in its own docblock, ScoutCheckInRollupQuery.php:19-47): keep BBOX_PAD_DEGREES (0.003 deg) prefiltering addresses before the geoDistance join; keep BOTH the `id IN (subquery)` prune on zod.public_address AND the INNER JOIN to address_links (dropping either either full-scans the 196M-row table or loses is_staged); parse EWKT with extract()+toFloat64OrNull, never readWKTPoint (which throws on a malformed row and ClickhouseQuery then silently empties the whole result); skip FINAL on the two zod CDC tables, relying on _peerdb_is_deleted=0 + DISTINCT instead.

Structural difference to account for when adapting the CTE: ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's left-hand side is clarity.scans_{hot,cold} FINAL WHERE org_id=? AND kit_id=? (integer keys); sc_positions has no org_id/kit_id column at all — it is ORDER BY (kit_mapping, timestamp_utc), string-keyed, and every reader wraps both sides in lower() (DEV-2012). This is not a drop-in table swap.

ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows \Throwable to [] only in production|testing; in local/other envs it re-throws (ClickhouseQuery.php:29-37). Every existing failure-mode test in the suite (an_org_enumeration_failure_skips_..., a_per_kit_failure_is_skipped_...) exploits this by flipping app.env to 'local' — any new AC7 test should follow the same pattern to actually reach the failure branch.

config/scout.php's own docblock states its no-fallback-default discipline exists specifically because 'DEV-2342 shipped one knob with three different defaults' in an earlier iteration of this same ticket — any new W3 tunable must follow the identical pattern (config is the single source of truth, no call-site fallback).

resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Current: O(addresses_per_org) x concurrency. $addresses held live across the 43-kit loop; array_chunk() copies the whole array once per kit; $matches[] accumulates unbounded. Measured: ~1.5-3 GB/process x 17 concurrent processes ~= 29 GB marginal footprint (evidence-38240-incident.md), against ~30 GB of host headroom. || W2 target: O(matches_per_cycle) x concurrency. Only ~40 match rows/cycle cross into PHP regardless of an org's address-book size (whether that org has 3 open addresses or the measured max of 296,459 on a single hotlist), so per-process memory should collapse to a small, near-constant footprint. W3's ceiling then bounds concurrency independent of runtime, so total memory becomes N_slots x O(matches) — small and capped — instead of the current unbounded product of an unbounded concurrency term against an already-large per-process term.
